craft_claim: Strategic intimate self-disclosure can be manufactured to simulate authenticity and increase persuasion, making the intimate tone a recurring vehicle for manipulation rather than candour.

supporting_evidence.location: Computers in Human Behavior 134: 107330, serial mediation results
supporting_evidence.note: Intimate self-disclosure increased perceived authenticity, which increased liking and ultimately message acceptance, demonstrating that disclosure can be used instrumentally to persuade.

supporting_evidence.location: New Media & Society 13(1): 114-133, on context collapse and the imagined audience
supporting_evidence.note: Social media collapse multiple audiences into one context, so a private-seeming register is broadcast; producers strategically convey authenticity while managing an imagined audience.
The para-social frame explains why a mediated speaker can appear intimate while the relationship remains commercially or rhetorically one-sided.

counterevidence.note: Audiences are not passive; they read authenticity as a performance and game it, so manufactured intimacy is unstable and easily detected.

scope: Marketing copy, influencer and brand address, political and advocacy messaging, and any first-person voice with a commercial or persuasive goal.
exceptions: Disclosure that imposes a real cost on the speaker and makes no request of the reader.
